references.text: The blood shall be a sign for you on the houses where you live. When I see the blood, I will pass over you (פָּסַח). This verse establishes the promise that verse 23 fulfills.
The instruction to smear blood on the doorposts and the upper lintel, which is what the LORD sees in verse 23.
The fulfillment of judgment: The LORD struck all the firstborn in Egypt, while the house of Israel was spared.
Moses announces that the LORD will go through (יֵצֵא) Egypt at midnight and strike down the firstborn.
The Egyptians buried their firstborn whom the LORD had struck among them; a reflection on this event.
The LORD of hosts will protect Jerusalem; He shall פָּסַח (pass over/protect) and deliver it. The same verb is used as in the Passover narrative.
A similar event where those with the mark are spared when the destroyer passes through Jerusalem.
The psalm describes how God sent destroying angels against Egypt and struck all the firstborn.
He struck all the firstborn in their land, the first of all their strength.
He who struck Egypt through their firstborn, for His mercy endures forever.
By faith Moses kept the Passover and sprinkled the blood, so that the destroyer (ὁ ὀλοθρεύων) would not touch their firstborn.
Christ, our Passover lamb (πάσχα), has been sacrificed. The connection between the Passover lamb and Christ's sacrifice.
Those who are sealed are protected from judgment, parallel to how the blood protected against the destroyer.
The statements are complementary parts of the same event; 12:12 establishes the target of judgment, while 12:23 establishes the mechanism of salvation.
A clear typological link where the temple ritual restores the function of the blood as a distinguishing mark between judgment and grace.
